caption: What if you travelled near light speed? Light covers about 300,000 km a second: 7.5 laps of Earth. Our fastest machine, NASA's Parker Solar Probe, hit about 690,000 km/h, still only about 0.064% of light speed. At 90% of light speed, your clock would tick less than half as fast as Earth's. At 99%, a round trip to Proxima Centauri (4.24 light-years away, our nearest star after the Sun) takes about 8.6 years on Earth but only about 1.2 years for you, so you'd return younger than your twin. At 99.9999%, one year on board equals about 707 years on Earth. CERN pushes protons to 99.9999991%, but 100% would need infinite energy. And it's real: muons made about 15 km up should decay within about 660 m, yet they reach the ground because their clocks run slow. Plot twist: it's a one-way ticket. Speed can skip you into the future, but physics has no known road back. Would YOU take the trip? 👇
